Their diet of fish includes smaller invertebrates as well as marine plankton. Kittiwakes spend winters primarily in the tropics and subtropics where large flocks may be encountered while performing some 110 000 km round-trips from breeding colonies in Scandinavia and the Atlantic Islands to the South-West Indian Ocean. Kittiwakers form mixed-species foraging flocks and their colonies tend to cluster in favourable locations near suitable feeding sites. During the peak breeding season (April to October in both hemispheres) males and females congregate at colonies to create a "pecking order" that is maintained throughout the year by displays of aggressive posturing.
